evidence_chain: [Fact] UTI describes itself as a workforce education provider for transportation, skilled trades, energy, and healthcare programs, with two reportable segments: UTI and Concorde Career Colleges. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] UTI says it offers most programs through hands-on labs, clinical placements, classroom delivery, and blended delivery models. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 UTI segment footprint: 15 campuses in nine states; Concorde footprint: 17 campuses in eight states and online. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 consolidated new student starts were 29,793, up 10.8%; average full-time active students were 24,618, up 10.5%; end-of-period full-time active students were 27,679, up 8.0%. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 UTI segment new student starts were 16,339, up 7.9%; Concorde new student starts were 13,454, up 14.5%. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 revenue was $835.6 million, up 14.0%; UTI revenue increased 11.4%; Concorde revenue increased 19.3%, primarily due to growth in full-time active students and new program expansions. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 included $42.0 million of cash capex primarily related to program expansions and maintenance capex; FY2026 guidance assumed approximately $100 million of cash capex, including new campus launches and program expansions. Source: FY2025 Q4/year-end release, https://investor.uti.edu/2025-11-19-Universal-Technical-Institute-Reports-Fiscal-Year-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-Results

[Fact] FY2026 Q1 average full-time active students were 26,858, up 7.2%; total new student starts were 5,449, up 2.6%; company reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance of $905-$915 million and new-student-start guidance of 31,500-33,000. Source: FY2026 Q1 release, https://investor.uti.edu/2026-02-04-Universal-Technical-Institute-Reports-Fiscal-Year-2026-First-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1

[Fact] FY2026 Q2 total new student starts were 7,569, up 13.8%; UTI starts were 4,110, up 14.5%; Concorde starts were 3,459, up 13.1%. Average full-time active students were 26,385, up 7.2%. Source: FY2026 Q2 release, https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-05/68422449-universal-technical-institute-inc-universal-technical-institute-reports-fiscal-year-2026-second-quarter-results-008.htm

[Fact] UTI offers manufacturer-paid MSAT programs tied to Mercedes-Benz, Peterbilt, Porsche, and Tesla START Collision, using vehicles, equipment, tools, and curricula provided by manufacturer brand partners. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] UTI also discloses student-paid manufacturer-specific programs involving BMW, Cummins, Daimler Trucks, Ford, GM, Mopar, Toyota, Honda, Harley-Davidson, Kawasaki, Mercury Marine, Suzuki, and Volvo Penta. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 disclosed growth projects include planned UTI Atlanta and UTI San Antonio campuses, a Dallas 30,000-square-foot expansion, Concorde Fort Myers co-branded with Heartland Dental, and a Concorde Aurora-to-Denver relocation to expand capacity. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 disclosed program expansions include HVACR launches, EV courses, new electrical programs, Tesla START Collision Repair, FirstCall Mechanical early-employment partnership, and Loftin Equipment early-employment partnership. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Fact] FY2025 10-K says approximately 78% of revenues, on a cash basis, came from Title IV Programs and various veterans’ programs, including approximately 43% from Direct Loan and approximately 23% from Pell. Source: FY2025 10-K, https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTI/10-k-universal-technical-institute-inc-files-annual-report-19df26f7e3b0.html

[Inference] The strongest current evidence supports demand and capacity expansion, not yet a proven moat. To upgrade, the research needs program-level utilization, placement/licensure, affordability, and employer-funded demand data.
falsification_plan: Falsify if FY2026/FY2027 student starts decelerate materially or turn negative despite new-campus and program-expansion spending.
Falsify if new campuses in Atlanta, San Antonio, Dallas expansion, Fort Myers/Heartland Dental, or Denver/Aurora relocation face repeated regulatory delays, under-enrollment, or high fixed-cost drag.
Falsify if Concorde’s healthcare starts grow but licensure pass rates, clinical placement access, graduate placement, or affordability metrics deteriorate.
Falsify if UTI’s automotive, diesel, EV, HVACR, electrical, robotics, aviation, welding, and energy programs fail to show employer demand beyond press-release-level partnerships.
Falsify if manufacturer-specific programs are not expanding seats, equipment access, funded training, dealer hiring pathways, or post-graduation employment outcomes.
Falsify if Title IV/gainful-employment/90-10/borrower-defense/accreditation changes become the dominant earnings driver and restrict student funding or program eligibility.
Falsify if growth capex and launch expenses persist without improving utilization, revenue per student, operating leverage, or free cash flow.
Falsify if student affordability pressures rise, evidenced by greater reliance on institutional financing, higher credit losses, weak collections, or poor debt-to-earnings disclosures.
Falsify if Reddit/student/graduate reputation checks and employer interviews consistently show poor training quality, low wage uplift, or graduates needing retraining elsewhere.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The key hidden supply-chain signal is whether physical capacity additions are filling with students and converting into employer-validated outcomes. Exact signals to verify: new-campus approval/opening cadence; Dallas expansion utilization; Atlanta and San Antonio campus ramp; Concorde Fort Myers/Heartland Dental ramp; Concorde Denver/Aurora relocation capacity; program launches in HVACR, EV, electrical, robotics/automation, wind and industrial maintenance; manufacturer-specific training seats; employer-sponsored training; clinical-site access; starts per program family; completion, placement, licensure pass rates, graduate wages, and affordability metrics.
next_research_tasks: Pull UTI’s latest FY2026 10-Q directly from SEC/EDGAR and reconcile Q2 starts, active students, revenue, operating expenses, capex, cash flow, and segment profitability.

Build a program-family tracker: transportation, diesel, aviation, welding, CNC/manufacturing, HVACR, electrical, robotics/automation, wind/energy, dental, nursing, diagnostic, surgical technology, respiratory therapy, physical therapist assistant.
For each major program family, collect starts, active students, tuition, duration, campus count, capacity, completion, placement, licensure pass rates, and graduate wage outcomes where disclosed.

Verify whether Atlanta, San Antonio, Dallas expansion, Fort Myers/Heartland Dental, and Denver/Aurora relocation have received required approvals, opened on schedule, and reached utilization milestones.
Check state and accreditor databases for campus/program approvals, probation, warning status, placement standards, and licensure exam outcomes.

Verify manufacturer partnerships by checking OEM/dealer sources, not only UTI disclosures: Mercedes-Benz, Peterbilt, Porsche, Tesla, BMW, Cummins, Daimler/Freightliner, Ford, GM, Toyota, Honda, Harley-Davidson, Kawasaki, Mercury Marine, Suzuki, Volvo Penta.
Conduct employer-demand validation: dealer networks, fleet operators, HVACR employers, aviation maintenance employers, dental groups, hospitals, imaging centers, and outpatient-care employers.

Quantify the federal-funding sensitivity: Title IV share, Pell exposure, Direct Loan exposure, VA/DOD/WIOA exposure, 90/10 compliance, gainful-employment risk by program, and OBBBA/ED rulemaking impact.

Compare UTI against reference leaders and adjacent public names such as Strategic Education and Grand Canyon Education only as context; keep UTI’s thesis separate because its exposure is more physical-capacity and hands-on-training driven.
Run a market-pricing check: market cap, EV/revenue, EV/EBITDA, free-cash-flow conversion, capex cycle, and short interest, without making any buy/sell recommendation.
Collect student/graduate reputation evidence from non-company sources and label it as weak/anecdotal unless supported by systematic outcomes data.
Interview or scrape local job postings near UTI/Concorde campuses to test whether employer demand maps to the exact programs being expanded.
risks: [Regulatory risk] Title IV, gainful employment, 90/10, borrower defense, accreditation, state authorization, veterans’ benefits, and Department of Education rulemaking are central risks because UTI depends heavily on federal and veteran-related funding.

[Affordability risk] FY2025 tuition ranges were high for some programs: UTI programs ranged from about $18,000 to $69,000; Concorde programs ranged from about $1,000 to $99,000. If graduate earnings or debt-to-earnings outcomes disappoint, demand and regulatory standing may weaken.

[Execution risk] FY2026 includes large growth investments and approximately $100 million planned capex. New campus or program delays, approval delays, slow utilization ramps, or instructor shortages could pressure margins and cash flow.
[Outcome risk] If completion, placement, licensure pass rates, graduate wages, or employer satisfaction weaken, the physical-capacity thesis becomes a volume-only enrollment story.
[Cyclicality risk] Student starts may be affected by macro conditions, unemployment, student willingness to incur debt, competition, and negative media around for-profit education.

[Healthcare-specific risk] Concorde growth depends on clinical placements, program approvals, healthcare faculty, local employer networks, licensure outcomes, and affordability; clinical-site constraints could cap growth.

[Partnership-quality risk] Manufacturer and employer partnerships may be valuable only if tied to funded seats, equipment, curriculum, hiring commitments, tuition reimbursement, or early employment—not merely brand marketing.
[Margin risk] Q1 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA declined due to strategic growth expenses; if growth investments fail to convert into starts and active students, the thesis weakens.

[Market-pricing risk] Although underfollowed relative to mega-cap education/software themes, UTI’s share price and valuation may already reflect some growth expectations; this report does not provide buy/sell advice or target prices.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver → skilled-labor shortages in transportation repair, diesel, aviation maintenance, manufacturing, HVACR, robotics/automation, energy, dental, nursing, diagnostic, and allied-health roles. Capacity bottleneck → accredited physical campuses, labs, vehicles/equipment, specialty tools, curricula, instructors, regulatory approvals, clinical/externship placements, career-services infrastructure, and employer/manufacturer relationships. UTI’s node → owner/operator of training campuses and employer-linked programs, positioned between students, OEMs/dealers, healthcare employers, clinical sites, regulators/accreditors, and federal/veteran/student-aid funding systems. Public-market mapping → UTI is not a software-like edtech name; it is closer to a regulated physical-capacity operator with education, labor-market, and financing risk.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: UTI 的 Serenity 线索在于实体职业教育产能：汽修、柴油、航空维修、焊接、CNC、HVACR、机器人自动化、电气、风电，以及 Concorde 的 allied healthcare 项目，均依赖校区、设备、实训工具、合格教师、临床/雇主关系、监管审批和本地就业管道。若 FY2026 以后新校区、新项目、Concorde 医疗项目和制造商/雇主合作持续带来学生 starts、活跃学生、就业结果和单位经济改善，UTI 可被视为技能短缺背景下较稀缺的线下培训产能平台。公司 FY2025 年报披露，UTI 经营 15 个校区，Concorde 经营 17 个校区；多数项目采用实验室、临床 placement、课堂和 blended delivery；FY2025 consolidated new student starts 为 29,793，同比增长 10.8%，average full-time active students 为 24,618，同比增长 10.5%。这些数据支持“实体产能正在扩张且需求仍在增长”的线索，但还不足以证明 UTI 拥有强定价权或不可替代瓶颈。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis] UTI’s Serenity angle is physical workforce-training capacity. Automotive, diesel, aviation maintenance, welding, CNC, HVACR, robotics/automation, electrical, wind power, and Concorde allied-health programs rely on campuses, equipment, hands-on labs, qualified instructors, clinical or externship access, employer relationships, regulatory approvals, and local placement networks. If post-FY2026 campus openings, program launches, Concorde healthcare growth, and employer/manufacturer partnerships keep translating into student starts, active-student growth, placement outcomes, and better unit economics, UTI may represent scarce hands-on training capacity tied to skilled-labor shortages. [Fact] UTI’s FY2025 10-K says the company operated 15 UTI campuses and 17 Concorde campuses, with most programs delivered through hands-on labs, clinical placements, classrooms, and blended models; FY2025 consolidated new student starts were 29,793, up 10.8%, and average full-time active students were 24,618, up 10.5%. [Inference] These disclosures support the idea that physical capacity is expanding and demand is still growing, but they do not yet prove durable pricing power or an unavoidable chokepoint.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: The market may categorize UTI as a for-profit vocational school exposed to student-start cycles, marketing efficiency, Title IV regulation, and student debt affordability. The hidden lens is that many of its programs are hard to replicate online because they require physical labs, equipment, local approvals, instructors, manufacturer-specific curricula, and employer or clinical placement relationships. This makes UTI more like a workforce-training infrastructure operator than a generic education enrollment story. Its current market cap is approximately $2.47 billion as of June 8, 2026, placing it in the preferred underfollowed small/mid-cap hunting range rather than the obvious mega-cap education/software lane.

summary: Bilingual Layer 5 mini deep report on Universal Technical Institute Inc. (UTI). Core conclusion: UTI remains an underfollowed Serenity/chokepoint candidate because its most interesting exposure is not generic education enrollment, but the operation and expansion of physical hands-on training capacity across transportation, skilled trades, energy, and allied healthcare. Evidence from FY2025 and FY2026 disclosures supports enrollment growth, campus/program expansion, manufacturer/employer partnerships, and a large physical-campus footprint. However, the thesis is still not upgraded to a high-confidence chokepoint conclusion because program-level placement, licensure, utilization, clinical-site capacity, pricing power, and student affordability outcomes need deeper verification.
